drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: Multi-agent research scenario. The system writes a report on electric bus adoption in European cities. The
drills.answer_line: SAM: Verification passes are useful, and it would catch some of these.
drills.stem: A report says electric bus adoption reached 31%, with no citation. One subagent found 31% in a ministry dataset from this year, another 22% in an industry survey from 2 years earlier. Each handed the synthesis agent a prose summary. Best fix?

options.A: Tell the synthesis agent to always prefer the most recent source and cite it
options.B: Subagents return claim-source mappings with excerpts and dates; report shows both figures with sources
options.C: Add a fact-checking subagent after synthesis that re-searches every statistic
options.D: Pass the full raw documents to the synthesis agent instead of summaries

drills.why: Prose summaries dropped attribution and dates, so fix the hand-off's structure. C is detective, after the damage; A imports newest-wins and hides the other figure.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. Multi-agent research scenario. The coordinator passes twelve
drills.answer_line: SAM: B is right. D is the miss. Instinct says a direct instruction fixes
drills.stem: The coordinator passes 12 long narrative document analysis reports, reasoning included, to the synthesis agent. Its context is nearly full, and its reports regularly omit findings from reports in the middle of the batch. Which two changes best address this?

options.A: Subagents return structured key facts with citations and relevance scores, not narrative reasoning
options.B: A key findings summary at the start of the input, and a section header for each subagent's detail
options.C: Increase max tokens on the synthesis call so it has room for all 12
options.D: Tell the synthesis agent to read every section with equal care, especially the middle ones
options.E: Truncate each report to its first 500 words so the batch fits

drills.why: Summary first and explicit headers fix position effects; structured upstream output fits a tight budget. D is a request, not a structural change; C caps output only.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Code generation scenario. After three hours exploring an unfamiliar
drills.answer_line: SAM: B. It persists findings, isolates the per-service exploration and
drills.stem: After 3 hours exploring an unfamiliar insurance platform, Claude Code contradicts earlier answers and describes "common approaches" rather than the modules it found. The next phase is a migration plan touching 4 services. What is the most effective approach?

options.A: Run /clear and re-explore from the beginning with a tighter prompt
options.B: Record findings in a scratchpad file; a subagent per service gets their summary; refer back later
options.C: Switch to a model with a larger context window and continue in the same session
options.D: Add a CLAUDE.md line telling Claude to always name specific classes

drills.why: B persists findings, isolates per-service exploration and injects the phase summary. A discards valid findings; C is scale instead of structure; D treats a symptom.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. Structured extraction scenario. A customs broker extracts
drills.answer_line: SAM: Both. A checks the segments the average hides, before automation.
drills.stem: A customs broker extracts shipment declarations. Validation accuracy is 97% overall, and the team plans to auto-approve every extraction with field confidence above 0.9. Which two steps should come with that change?

options.A: Measure accuracy by document type and field on labelled data; confirm every segment first
options.B: After launch, review a stratified random sample of auto-approved extractions
options.C: Auto-approve now, because 97% beats the human team's measured accuracy
options.D: Ask the model to re-check any extraction it rated above 0.9 before approval
options.E: Review only the lowest-confidence 10% of extractions from now on

drills.why: A checks the segments the average hides, before automation. B keeps measuring error rates after it. C trusts the aggregate the guide warns about.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Multi-agent research scenario. A document analysis subagent finds that
drills.answer_line: SAM: That is miss pattern five, importing a constraint the stem never stated.
drills.stem: A document analysis subagent finds that two credible industry reports give different figures for the same market's size in the same year. What should it do?

options.A: Report the figure from the more recently published report
options.B: Return both figures with sources, excerpts and dates, marked conflicting; coordinator reconciles
options.C: Leave the market size out of its output, since the value is uncertain
options.D: Report the average of the two figures with both sources cited

drills.why: Conflict included, annotated, coordinator decides. A imports a constraint; C is silent suppression; D invents a number neither source reported.

drills.question_line: SAM: Before we finish, your turn. Pause and name the four task statements we covered, with
drills.answer_line: ALEX: Long interactions, giveaway "exact" or "the customer later disputes".
drills.prompt: Name the four task statements covered, with the giveaway word for each.
drills.answer: Long interactions ("exact", "the customer later disputes"); codebase exploration ("typical patterns"); human review ("97% overall"); provenance ("two credible sources").

In this episode: Keep exact amounts, dates and order numbers alive in long conversations
Trim tool output before it floods the context
Spot context degradation; scratchpad file, subagents or /compact
When confident extractions can skip human review, and keep checking them
Carry sources and conflicting figures intact through a multi-agent report
Cold open: the uncited statistic: Report states 31% adoption with no citation; another source said 22%
Task statements 5.1, 5.4, 5.5 and 5.6; 15% domain, primary for 4 scenarios
Progressive summarisation loses amounts, dates and customer expectations
Persistent case facts block in every prompt, outside summarised history
Trim verbose tool output to relevant fields in code, before it lands
Lost in the middle: key findings summary first, explicit section headers
Segment two: context degradation: Symptoms: inconsistent answers, "typical patterns" instead of found classes
Scratchpad file keeps findings across context boundaries
Subagents explore specific questions and return condensed summaries
Subagents inherit nothing: inject a phase summary into their prompt
/compact for verbose discovery output; findings stay on disk
Crash recovery: agents export state; coordinator loads a manifest
Segment three: aggregate accuracy: 97% overall can hide 78% on one document type or field
Verify accuracy by document type and field before automating
Field-level confidence calibrated on a labelled validation set
Raw self-reported confidence with a fixed cut-off is the distractor
Stratified random sample of high-confidence output: error rates, new patterns
Segment four: provenance: Attribution is lost when findings are compressed without their source
Structured claim-source mappings: claim, source, excerpt, date
Conflicting credible sources: annotate both, coordinator reconciles
Check dates first: a temporal difference is not a conflict
Separate established from contested findings; keep methodological context
Render by content type: tables, prose, structured lists
Cold open: the verdict: Answer: B, structured claim-source mappings with dates, preserved
Fact-checking subagent is detective, after attribution is already lost
"Newest wins" imports a rule and hides the other figure
Raw documents give synthesis more middle to lose things in
Five to remember: Exact figures, dates, IDs in a persistent case facts block; trim tool results before they pile up
Lost in the middle: key findings first and section headers; tight budget: structured upstream output
"Typical patterns" means degradation: scratchpad, subagents with summaries, /compact, manifests
Aggregate accuracy hides weak segments: check by type and field, calibrate, stratified sampling
Claim-source mappings with dates survive synthesis; conflicts annotated, coordinator reconciles
Recap: the exam tells: If a figure, date or order number disappears after summarisation, a case facts block
If tool results pile up with unused fields, trim them in code before they land
If middle findings go missing, key findings summary first and section headers
If downstream context is nearly full, structured upstream output, not bigger max tokens
If Claude Code cites typical patterns and contradicts itself, scratchpad, subagents, /compact
If high overall accuracy tempts dropping review, segment accuracy, calibrate, stratified sample
If an option uses raw self-rated confidence with a fixed cut-off, it loses
If a number is uncited or sources disagree, claim-source mappings with dates, annotate conflict
